subject: DPA redline coverage, SCCs & role split — exec approval path
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline coverage, SCCs & role split — exec approval path

Karen — thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached are the initial redlines from our side (redlines_jonas_20280305.pdf). Key asks from our side summarized below: 

1) Role split: we propose Processor responsibilities in the Order Form (Schedule B) map to the ‘hosting and inference’ components only; anything related to customer-provided data transformation at rest would be scoped to the Controller (your side) unless you want Redwood to accept narrower processor obligations in Exhibit X.

2) SCCs: we can adopt the updated EU SCCs but need to confirm encryption-at-rest and KMS key custody language — Laura, please see paragraph 4 on page 3 of the attachment.

3) Transfer impact addendum: NovaMed indicated they need an explicit transfer-addendum that lists permitted cross-border flows, and a fallback routing policy if UK/EU to US processing is blocked. We can offer a routing fallback to our EU Dedicated cluster for a surcharge; Ben, can you confirm pricing delta?

Next steps we need from NovaMed: a redline of the DPA with your proposed controller/processor split and any KMS custody preferences. If acceptable, we’ll need executive approval to proceed with the addendum and a short exec call to sign off on surcharge and SLA exception (if any).

Proposed cadence: your redline by Wed 3/7 -> legal sync w/ Redwood by Thu 3/8 -> exec decision Fri 3/9.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Cloud Contracts (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_jonas_20280305.pdf
From: Karen Liu <karen@novamed.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rios <tom.rios@gcp-proc.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 11:31:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline coverage, SCCs & role split — exec approval path

Jonas — thanks for sending this through and for the clear summary. I attached our annotated DPA extract (novamed_comments_20280306.docx) with a few clarifications: 

- We accept the processor-controller split in principle but need Redwood to accept a short clause requiring retention of audit logs for 2 years and a monthly attestation that subprocessor lists are accurate.
- On KMS: NovaMed prefers customer-managed keys (BYOK) for UK/EU-hosted workloads. If we can’t do BYOK in your hosted environment, please confirm the exact encryption controls and whether HSM-backed KMS in the EU cluster is available.
- Transfer-addendum: we will flag a hard stop for transfers to the US unless there’s an approved legal basis; the fallback to EU Dedicated is acceptable but we need pricing and timeline.

We don’t expect many changes to the MSA besides the DPA appendix, but we will also loop in Procurement (Tom) for the surcharge/ordering path. Our legal also flagged that the SCCs reference needs to include the latest 2021 modular clauses (our counsel will attach specific language if needed).

Can you confirm: 
- who at Redwood will produce the formal transfer-addendum draft?
- is there an internal SLA exception form we need to fill for BYOK or KMS exceptions?

I’ll aim to have our redline by EOD Wed.

Best,
Karen Liu
VP Legal 
NovaMed

Attachment: novamed_comments_20280306.docx

Subject: Re: DPA redline coverage, SCCs & role split — exec approval path

Folks — reviewed Karen’s notes and the attached. High-level legal comments: 

- Audit logs: Redwood can commit to a 2-year retention for the audit trail relevant to the MSA operations (access logs, export events) but we should exclude ephemeral infra logs. I’ll upload a short clause for Exhibit C.
- BYOK: BYOK is non-trivial for our hosted SaaS; we can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted (Redwood API), we offer HSM-backed keys in our EU cluster but not BYOK — we should offer a transitional control: pre-boot encryption key escrow with quarterly attestations.
- SCCs: we will accept the 2021 modular clauses but need to add a limited liability carve-out for processing activities outside the agreed scope (e.g., experimentation, non-production training).

Procurement question for Ben: if NovaMed accepts EU Dedicated fallback, what is the approximate monthly surcharge for reserved capacity for an enterprise order of their size (estimate attached)? Need a ballpark so we can present to NovaMed execs.

Action items I’ll own: draft Exhibit C audit clause and SCC insertion language by EOD Thu 3/8. Jonas — please confirm who will present to NovaMed execs and whether we want a 30-minute decision window or a 60-minute walkthrough.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

2) Ben to confirm surcharge ballpark by EOD Fri (Ben, please reply to this thread).
3) NovaMed to confirm redline by close of day Mon 3/12 if possible; if we have Karen’s redline earlier we can speed the route.

I’ve scheduled a 30-minute exec decision slot for Fri 3/16 at 09:00 CET (link in HubSpot). Goal: one-way approve redline + surcharge and sign the transfer-addendum via DocuSign same day. If procurement needs more time we’ll convert to a 60-minute session.

Action items for this thread:
